libraries.name: shadcn/ui
libraries.tagline: This is not a component library. It is how you build your component library.
libraries.description: A set of ready-made interface pieces, like buttons and popups, that get copied straight into your project so you own the code. Instead of fighting a package's styles, you edit the components directly to match your app.

libraries.name: Chakra UI
libraries.tagline: Chakra UI is a component system for building products with speed
libraries.description: A toolkit of ready-to-use building blocks for React apps, with sensible styling out of the box and built-in dark mode. Colors, spacing, and variants are tweaked through one central theme system.
libraries.free_note: The core library is free under MIT; Chakra Pro (prebuilt templates) is a separate paid product.

libraries.name: Mantine
libraries.tagline: A fully featured React components library
libraries.description: A big collection of React building blocks plus handy hooks for things like forms and notifications, with light and dark themes built in. Everything is customizable and free to use in any project, even commercial ones.

libraries.name: MUI (Material UI)
libraries.tagline: Material UI: React components that implement Material Design
libraries.description: A large, battle-tested set of ready-styled React components based on Google's Material Design look. A great fit if you want a complete, polished design out of the box with plenty of examples to copy from.
libraries.free_note: MUI Core, including Material UI, is free under MIT; MUI also sells separate paid add-ons such as MUI X Pro.

libraries.name: Radix UI
libraries.tagline: An open-source UI component library for building high-quality, accessible design systems and web apps.
libraries.description: Plain, unstyled building blocks like dialogs and menus that handle all the tricky interaction and accessibility work for you. You add your own styling, so they can look like anything you want.
libraries.free_note: There is no single install: each component is its own package, so you install only the primitives you need.

libraries.name: Headless UI
libraries.tagline: A set of completely unstyled, fully accessible UI components, designed to integrate beautifully with Tailwind CSS.
libraries.description: Unstyled interactive pieces from the Tailwind CSS team, made to pair perfectly with Tailwind classes. All the keyboard and screen reader behavior is handled, while you control every pixel of the look.

libraries.name: Ark UI
libraries.tagline: A headless library with 45+ accessible components. Bring your own styles and build a design system that works across React, Solid, Vue, and Svelte.
libraries.description: Unstyled, accessibility-first building blocks from the Chakra UI team that work the same way across React, Vue, Solid, and Svelte. You bring the styles; Ark handles the complex interaction logic underneath.

libraries.name: HeroUI
libraries.tagline: An open-source UI component library for building beautiful and accessible user interfaces.
libraries.description: A polished, ready-to-use set of React components (formerly called NextUI) that look good with zero styling effort and are accessible by default. Built on Tailwind CSS and Adobe's React Aria, so it is fast and works with modern React.
libraries.free_note: Free and open source; the repo LICENSE file states MIT, though the docs FAQ mentions Apache 2.0.

libraries.name: Ant Design
libraries.tagline: An enterprise-class design system for building modern, intelligent, and delightful user experiences.
libraries.description: A huge set of ready-made building blocks like buttons, forms, and tables for React apps, made by Alibaba's design team. A great pick when you want a polished, professional look without designing every piece yourself.

libraries.name: PrimeReact
libraries.tagline: The ultimate collection of design-agnostic, flexible and accessible React UI Components.
libraries.description: Over 90 React components, from basic inputs to full data tables and dialogs, with themes you can restyle to match your brand. It is built by PrimeTek, the team behind several well-known UI kits.

libraries.name: React Bootstrap
libraries.tagline: The most popular front-end framework rebuilt for React.
libraries.description: Bootstrap's familiar components rebuilt as proper React components, so you get the classic Bootstrap look without fiddling with jQuery. A safe, well-documented choice if you already know Bootstrap.

libraries.name: Grommet
libraries.tagline: Focus on the essential experience.
libraries.description: A clean React toolkit from HPE that keeps things simple and works well for everyone, including people using screen readers. It has strong theming tools so you can reshape the look easily.

libraries.name: Vuetify
libraries.tagline: A Vue Component Framework
libraries.description: A full collection of Vue components in the Material Design style, so your app looks like a polished Google-style product. It needs no design skills and handles layout, themes, and responsive design for you.

libraries.name: Quasar
libraries.tagline: Build high-performance Vue.js user interfaces in record time.
libraries.description: A Vue framework that goes beyond components: write one codebase and ship it as a website, a mobile app, or a desktop app. Great if you want your project on many platforms without starting over.

libraries.name: Element Plus
libraries.tagline: A Vue 3 based component library for designers and developers.
libraries.description: A complete Vue 3 component library with a friendly, rounded look and full TypeScript support. Popular for admin dashboards and business apps where you need a lot of form and table components.

libraries.name: Naive UI
libraries.tagline: A Vue 3 component library: fairly complete, theme customizable, uses TypeScript, fast
libraries.description: Over 90 ready-made pieces like buttons, menus, and data tables for Vue 3 apps. You restyle everything with one theme file instead of touching CSS, and it stays quick even with long lists.

libraries.name: DaisyUI
libraries.tagline: The most popular, free and open-source Tailwind CSS component library
libraries.description: A plugin for Tailwind CSS that adds ready-made components like buttons, cards, and menus. You use short, readable class names instead of writing every style by hand.

libraries.name: Flowbite
libraries.tagline: Build websites even faster with components on top of Tailwind CSS
libraries.description: Over 56 ready-made components like buttons, navbars, and modals built on Tailwind CSS. Interactive pieces like dropdowns run on small JavaScript snippets, so it works with almost any setup.
libraries.free_note: Core component library is MIT licensed and free; a separate paid Pro pack adds more prebuilt pages and layouts.

libraries.name: Preline UI
libraries.tagline: An open-source set of prebuilt UI components based on Tailwind CSS
libraries.description: Prebuilt buttons, forms, navbars, modals, and more that layer on top of Tailwind CSS. Everything is styled with Tailwind classes, so you can restyle pieces to match your own brand fast.
libraries.free_note: Dual-licensed MIT and Preline UI Fair Use License; components are free for personal and commercial use but may not be redistributed as-is or used for a competing product.

libraries.name: Bulma
libraries.tagline: Free, open source, and modern CSS framework based on Flexbox
libraries.description: A CSS-only styling framework, so there is no JavaScript to learn. Simple class names style buttons, forms, and page columns, and it drops into any JavaScript setup.

libraries.name: UIkit
libraries.tagline: A lightweight and modular front-end framework for developing fast and powerful web interfaces
libraries.description: A small, complete front-end kit with more than 70 styled components plus a grid system and animations. It works with plain HTML and any JavaScript framework.

libraries.name: Web Awesome
libraries.tagline: The open source library of web components from Font Awesome
libraries.description: Ready-made web components like buttons, dialogs, inputs, and tooltips from the makers of Font Awesome. Since they are web components, they drop into any project or framework.
libraries.free_note: Core library is MIT licensed and fully free; Web Awesome Pro is a separate paid add-on with extra components and asset packs.

libraries.name: Gluestack UI
libraries.tagline: React and React Native UI components library for web and mobile apps
libraries.description: A copy-paste component library for React and React Native apps, styled with Tailwind CSS. Grab ready-made buttons, forms, and screens, then restyle everything to match your brand.

libraries.name: Tamagui
libraries.tagline: React Native UI kit with copy-paste composable components
libraries.description: A styling library and UI kit that lets you share one codebase between web and mobile apps. It compiles your styles into fast, platform-perfect output automatically.

libraries.name: React Native Paper
libraries.tagline: Making your React Native apps look and feel native
libraries.description: Google's Material Design packaged for React Native, from the team at Callstack. Ready-made buttons, cards, dialogs, and more that feel at home on iOS and Android, with theming and accessibility built in.

libraries.name: Carbon Design System
libraries.tagline: IBM's open source design system for products and digital experiences
libraries.description: IBM's free design system: a full kit of building blocks from colors and type to buttons and data tables. It powers IBM's own products and is open for anyone to use.

libraries.name: Fluent UI
libraries.tagline: Microsoft's design system and component set for building apps in the Microsoft 365 style
libraries.description: Microsoft's free UI toolkit: ready-made React components, design tokens, and icons that fit right in with Teams and Office. Accessibility and theming come built in.
libraries.free_note: The code is MIT licensed, but Fluent UI fonts and icons are covered by separate asset terms.

libraries.name: React Spectrum
libraries.tagline: Build Once. Adapt Everywhere.
libraries.description: Adobe's collection of ready-made interface pieces with accessibility baked in. Dark mode, touch support, and right-to-left languages are all handled for you.

libraries.name: Lightning Design System
libraries.tagline: The CSS framework behind the Salesforce look and feel
libraries.description: Salesforce's free design system: ready-to-use markup, CSS, and design patterns for apps that should look and feel like Salesforce. Official React components are available too.
